evidence.claim: Buhari signed the 2022 Appropriation Bill and 2021 Finance Bill into law, restoring a predictable January-to-December fiscal year, while asking for amendment and virement because the National Assembly had altered many projects and allocations.
evidence.title: President Buhari Signs N17.127tr 2022 Budget Into Law, Directs MDAs to Commence Early Preparation of 2023 Transition Budget
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the 2022 Appropriation Bill and 2021 Finance Bill into law, restoring a predictable January-to-December fiscal year, while asking for amendment and virement because the National Assembly had altered many projects and allocations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official record of the president's fiscal act and stated concerns about budget changes.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 enactment that governed the 2022 fiscal framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler action, though the resulting budget also reflects National Assembly amendments and inherited fiscal constraints.
contrary_evidence: The president said the enacted budget still needed amendment/virement, suggesting implementation friction rather than a clean policy win.

evidence.claim: Buhari approved the appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as NBS Statistician-General and CEO; the notice describes him as a professional statistician with more than three decades of experience and prior NBS leadership roles.
evidence.title: President Buhari Approves Appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as Statistician-General of the Federation and Chief Executive Officer of the National Bureau of Statistics
evidence.excerpt: Buhari approved the appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as NBS Statistician-General and CEO; the notice describes him as a professional statistician with more than three decades of experience and prior NBS leadership roles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official appointment notice with a direct attribution and a specific technocratic résumé.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 appointment relevant to data capacity and evidence-based policy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler action, though one technocratic appointment does not prove the quality of the broader economic team.
contrary_evidence: A single technocratic appointment does not offset other evidence of politicization in economic offices.

evidence.claim: Buhari framed 2022 tax policy around stable domestic revenue mobilization, tax harmonization, clearer FIRS authority, and improved tax-to-GDP performance, while saying the 2021 tax dialogue influenced policy and administrative changes and FIRS surpassed its 2021 collection target.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Address at the 2nd National Tax Dialogue Week
evidence.excerpt: Buhari framed 2022 tax policy around stable domestic revenue mobilization, tax harmonization, clearer FIRS authority, and improved tax-to-GDP performance, while saying the 2021 tax dialogue influenced policy and administrative changes and FIRS surpassed its 2021 collection target.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech, but self-reported success and goals need outside corroboration for execution claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari policy direction through tax administration; execution attribution is partial because outcomes also depend on the revenue authority and broader macro conditions.
contrary_evidence: World Bank and IMF later described Nigeria's revenue base as very weak and fiscal space constrained.
The speech is aspirational and does not itself prove sustained implementation.

evidence.claim: Buhari said his administration's fight against corruption was a cardinal reform pillar and linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, while urging ICPC action on sexual harassment in education.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the 4th National Summit on Diminishing Corruption in the Public Sector
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said his administration's fight against corruption was a cardinal reform pillar and linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, while urging ICPC action on sexual harassment in education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Buhari speech with clear stated priorities, but it is mainly rhetoric and only limited execution evidence sits in the speech itself.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari statement and reform signal; actual anti-corruption performance needs independent corroboration.
contrary_evidence: The speech is aspirational and does not by itself show results.
Other evidence shows ongoing corruption and fiscal leakage.

evidence.claim: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022 and said a fund would cover 83 million poor Nigerians, using a vulnerable-group fund, digital records, and state-federal implementation coordination.
evidence.title: In Bid to Achieve Universal Coverage, President Buhari Signs National Health Authority Bill Into Law
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022 and said a fund would cover 83 million poor Nigerians, using a vulnerable-group fund, digital records, and state-federal implementation coordination.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential action with a concrete institutional reform and target population, though delivery still depends on implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari enactment through presidential assent; implementation is shared with the health ministry, states, and the new authority.
contrary_evidence: Coverage promises do not prove actual enrollment or service quality in 2022.
The program is partly an institutional design rather than a completed outcome.

evidence.claim: Buhari described the humanitarian ministry as a strategic intervention and listed IDP, flood-response, disability, aging, poverty-reduction, and social-investment frameworks as part of a plan to lift 100 million Nigerians out of poverty in 10 years.
evidence.title: Humanitarian Issues: President Buhari Urges More Private Sector Participation, Highlights Intervention Programmes
evidence.excerpt: Buhari described the humanitarian ministry as a strategic intervention and listed IDP, flood-response, disability, aging, poverty-reduction, and social-investment frameworks as part of a plan to lift 100 million Nigerians out of poverty in 10 years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential account of policy architecture, but most of the evidence is self-description rather than independent evaluation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari framing of the administration's social-protection and humanitarian program; delivery responsibility is shared with the ministry, agencies, states, and partners.
contrary_evidence: The ministry was created in 2019, so much of the structure predates 2022.
A stated framework is not proof of effective delivery.

evidence.claim: ASUU suspended its eight-month strike after appeals from President Buhari and others, and Reuters noted the government had set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.
evidence.title: Nigeria's public university lecturers suspend strike after eight months
evidence.excerpt: ASUU suspended its eight-month strike after appeals from President Buhari and others, and Reuters noted the government had set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters report text in article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated reporting on a major implementation failure and the government's response; the suspension does not prove the dispute was solved.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Buhari's appeal and budget response are directly attributable, but the strike also reflected entrenched labor disputes and university-funding structure.
contrary_evidence: The union said issues were not satisfactorily resolved.
The dispute had been ongoing for months, so suspension was not full execution of a reform plan.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Buhari decision on nuclear brinkmanship, command-and-control, or other existential-risk use of presidential authority.
No independent audit of whether the 2021-2022 safeguards and physical-protection framework was actually implemented in practice.
No direct evidence of Buhari personally directing external military operations, proxy conduct, or coercive cross-border action in 2022.
No substantive mediation track or concrete ceasefire result led by Buhari himself.
Independent, case-level follow-through on prosecutions and investigations for major 2022 abuses is thin.
Some severe insecurity items are still better understood as state failure in a violent environment than as direct ruler-directed violence.
No independent pre-election audit of how fully the Electoral Act 2022 was implemented before the 2023 polls.
Much of the affirmative evidence is self-description from Buhari and his administration.
Budget execution and capital-spending delivery are not independently audited at the project level here.
Household-level and regional distributional causality remains only partially evidenced.
Independent audit evidence on how much of the announced welfare and health delivery actually reached beneficiaries in 2022 is limited.
The chapter still mixes federal action, donor support, and inherited deprivation.
No direct 2022 evidence of Buhari's assets, procurement benefits, bribes, or formal audit/court findings tied to personal enrichment.
The family-appointment case is strong on patronage but still thin on Buhari's knowledge, benefit, and intent beyond approval.
The Lake Chad arms claim is shown as unsupported, but there is no public correction or retraction by Buhari in the package.
Independent audit-grade evidence on the delivery tracker and the administration's correction of weak implementers is still limited.
The chapter still depends heavily on macro outcomes that mix Buhari-era policy with inherited constraints and external shocks.
